thread:
matt: FYI noticed a p99 spike on /v1/generate at ~23:00 UTC. baseline p99 ~1.8s, spikes to ~6.2s on a subset of shards. suspect interaction between microbatching and some very long max_tokens requests. attaching quick repro in the thread.
zlata: Can you paste the perf slice + which kernel path was taken? :thinking:
priya: I pulled the profiler for the slow shard — main signal: kernel selection fell back to non-fused GEMM for the attention matmul when microbatch size == 1, plus extra KV cache misses when seq_len > 1024. snippet:
```
PROFILE: model=BLOOM-like shard=3
  attention_kernel: chosen=matmul_scalar_fallback (cost 12.4ms)
  kv_cache_hits=0.68 kv_evictions=3
  microbatch_size=1 mean_latency=620ms tail=3.9s
```
priya: Also saw heavy variance when requests had max_tokens 2048. the runtime does recompute some past attention when cache evicted, which amplifies the tail.
kevin: Two quick mitigations we can try in order of effort:
 1) per-route microbatch cap (microbatch_max=8) to avoid tiny single-item kernels
 2) per-route max_tokens cap for interactive routes (256 or 512)
 3) add route-level timeout_ms (e.g., 3500) + truncation policy to drop oldest context instead of letting request blow past SLO.
kevin: Example route snippet we can canary:
```
route:
  path: "/v1/generate"
  microbatch_max: 8
  max_tokens: 256
  timeout_ms: 3500
  truncation: truncate_left  # drop oldest tokens when input+max_tokens would exceed limit
  kernel_preference: [quantized_fused, fused, default]
```
alice: Important: kernel_preference ordering is key. prefer quantized_fused first, then fused, then fallback. we should avoid matmul_scalar_fallback unless nothing else matches. also consider a dedicated slow-request pool: if user requests max_tokens>512, route to Dedicated or deprioritize.
zlata: I want to be careful about changing microbatch_max globally — can we make it dynamic per-model and per-route? some models benefit from bigger microbatches. propose dynamic_max_microbatch: based on recent seq_len distribution and token_rate.
kevin: yep, dynamic per-model is doable. short-term: per-route override is fastest for rollout.
priya: For observability: add histogram of kernel_choice vs latency, and kv_eviction_count correlated with tail. I added a quick dashboard query:
```
SELECT histogram(latency), group_by(kernel_choice), filter(kv_eviction_count > 0)
```
priya: This caught the spike — eviction_count correlated strongly with >3s tails.
matt: OK. Plan: canary the route snippet (kevin) to 5% on us-west for 1h, watch p95/p99 + kernel_choice histogram. if tail reduces, roll to 50% then global. create follow-up RFI ticket.
alice: Also want to add adaptive truncation: if projected latency > threshold, reduce max_tokens for that request automatically (soft cap). we should surface that in logs with reason code.
kevin: I'll open canary PR and add telemetry alerts: p95 > 2s or p99 > 4s => rollback. also alert on % requests hitting truncation.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary routes/1847-microbatch-cap @ 5% (us-west) :rocket:
deploy-bot: Canary finished: success (0 errors), metrics: p95 down 12%, p99 down 40% on canary shards :shipit:
matt: Nice. next actions: (1) make microbatch cap configurable per-model (2) implement kernel preference ordering in selector (3) add per-route truncation + timeout defaults (256/3500ms) (4) follow-up perf run for long-seq repro and KV eviction tuning. created ticket RFI-927 to track.
zlata: I'll dump a longer repro script for the perf run — will include varying seq_len and random eviction triggers.
priya: I'll add the kernel/histogram telemetry and correlate with quantized kernel usage.
alice: I'll draft operator docs for truncation policies and recommended defaults for interactive vs batch routes.
kevin: early wins look promising. thanks team. :tada:
